sk-cd7f4cd1.stem: What are the three parts of the sternum?
options: Jugular notch, angle and xiphoid process
Body, xiphoid process and jugular notch
sk-cd7f4cd1.explanation: From top to bottom the sternum consists of the manubrium, the body and the xiphoid process. The junction of manubrium and body is the sternal angle (level of the 2nd rib).

sk-0a8d84f1.stem: Which is the only bone of the arm?
sk-0a8d84f1.explanation: Only the humerus lies in the arm (brachium); the radius and ulna are in the forearm and the clavicle and scapula in the shoulder girdle.

sk-b53d9bdb.stem: Which bone lies on the thumb side of the forearm?
sk-b53d9bdb.explanation: In the anatomical position the radius lies on the lateral (thumb) side of the forearm and the ulna on the medial (little finger) side.

sk-02299d72.stem: With which bone does the medial end of the clavicle articulate?
sk-02299d72.explanation: The medial end of the clavicle forms the sternoclavicular joint with the manubrium; the lateral end forms the acromioclavicular joint with the acromion.

sk-dc65dbda.stem: The acromion is part of which bone?
sk-dc65dbda.explanation: The acromion is the lateral end of the spine of the scapula; it forms the highest bony point of the shoulder and articulates with the clavicle.

sk-135626d7.stem: In which hollow of the scapula does the head of the humerus sit at the shoulder joint?
sk-135626d7.explanation: The head of the humerus forms the shoulder (glenohumeral) joint with the glenoid cavity of the scapula; the socket is deepened by the glenoid labrum.

sk-1a79acf4.stem: The olecranon, felt at the back of the elbow, belongs to which bone?
sk-1a79acf4.explanation: The olecranon is the projection at the proximal end of the ulna; with the elbow extended it enters the olecranon fossa of the humerus, and triceps brachii attaches to it.

sk-1924a576.stem: How many carpal bones are there in the wrist?
sk-1924a576.explanation: The carpal bones are eight short bones in two rows: proximally scaphoid, lunate, triquetrum, pisiform; distally trapezium, trapezoid, capitate, hamate.

sk-cc283b3f.stem: How many phalanges does the thumb have?
sk-cc283b3f.explanation: The thumb has two phalanges (proximal and distal) and the other fingers three each; the hand has 14 phalanges in total.

sk-766cdcb8.stem: Which three bones form the hip bone?
sk-766cdcb8.explanation: The hip bone forms from the ilium, ischium and pubis fusing at the acetabulum; fusion is completed at puberty as the Y-shaped cartilage ossifies.

sk-e8ec8422.stem: Which bony prominence carries the body weight when sitting?
sk-e8ec8422.explanation: When sitting, weight rests on the ischial tuberosities. The hamstring muscles also arise from them.

sk-fce811c8.stem: Which thick, weight-bearing bone lies on the inner side of the leg?
sk-fce811c8.explanation: The tibia (shinbone) is the thick bone on the inner side of the leg and carries most of the weight; the thin fibula on the outer side contributes little to weight-bearing.

sk-3d64e2a3.explanation: The patella develops within the quadriceps femoris tendon and is the largest sesamoid bone of the body.

sk-51c47666.stem: To which bone does the bony bump on the outer side of the ankle (lateral malleolus) belong?
sk-51c47666.explanation: The outer ankle bump is the lateral malleolus, the lower end of the fibula; the inner bump is the medial malleolus of the tibia. The lateral malleolus reaches lower than the medial.

sk-5b89ff5c.explanation: The calcaneus is the largest tarsal bone and forms the heel; the Achilles tendon attaches to its calcaneal tuberosity behind.

sk-617628de.stem: How many bones are there in each foot?
sk-617628de.explanation: Each foot has 26 bones: 7 tarsals, 5 metatarsals and 14 phalanges (not counting sesamoids).

sk-4ce46011.stem: Which tarsal bone lies in front of the calcaneus on the outer border of the foot?
sk-4ce46011.explanation: The cuboid lies in front of the calcaneus on the outer border of the foot and articulates with the 4th–5th metatarsals; the navicular lies in front of the talus on the inner side.

sk-62a44079.stem: What is the basic structural unit of compact bone?
sk-62a44079.explanation: Compact bone is built of osteons, lamellae arranged in rings around a central Haversian canal. Spongy bone is made of trabeculae.

sk-ef479b99.stem: What are the collagen fibres that bind the periosteum firmly to bone and penetrate it called?
sk-ef479b99.explanation: Sharpey's (perforating) fibres are thick collagen bundles passing from the periosteum into the bone matrix; they also anchor tendons and ligaments to bone.

sk-545c3b65.stem: By which process do the bones of the skull vault (calvaria) ossify?
sk-545c3b65.explanation: The skull vault, the facial bones and most of the clavicle develop directly from mesenchyme by intramembranous ossification. The skull base, vertebrae and most limb bones ossify on a cartilage model (endochondral).

sk-64644656.stem: An X-ray of which region is most often used to assess bone age?
sk-64644656.explanation: Bone age is determined by comparing the appearance of the ossification centres and the state of the growth plates on an X-ray of the left hand and wrist with standard atlases (Greulich–Pyle).

sk-7f45caa6.stem: In adults, where are bone marrow aspiration and biopsy most often performed?
options: Posterior iliac crest (around the posterior superior iliac spine)
sk-7f45caa6.explanation: In adults the posterior iliac crest is preferred because it is both safe and rich in red marrow. The proximal tibia is used in small children.
